AccountLabel.description: An account label from deck config.

address.description: The mailbox's address (`you@example.com`): the web app's "View email" opens a card's thread in Gmail with it.

Action.description: One proposed action. The `type` tag is also the name `runner.eligible` uses.

oneOf.description: Out of spam and back into the inbox: Gmail's "Not spam".
Pass the email on to a session, with the fixed forward header.

note.description: The user's own comment, set on a sent row. Part of the approved payload, not an adjustment.

oneOf.description: A Gmail draft in the thread, which the user edits and sends themselves. The normal reply path.

from.description:
The address it's sent from. Must be one the account can send as (checked when the card is posted, again
before sending, and against the sent message's From header afterwards).

requested_by.description: The session that asked for the draft, which gets what the user really sent (the sent-mail forward).

oneOf.description: Sends straight away. Never runner-eligible.

from.description:
The address it's sent from. Must be one the account can send as (checked when the card is posted, again
before sending, and against the sent message's From header afterwards).

requested_by.description: The session that asked for the draft, which gets what the user really sent (the sent-mail forward).

oneOf.description:
A tracker story: create one, or comment on one. Boards are names from deck config; the runner's and the skill's
own config map them to the tracker's IDs.
Message, wrap up or close another session (the Work tab's session actions).

ActionRecord.description: An action as stored on a card version.

outcome.description: What was sent and what came back.

ActionReport.description: One action's result, for `quietdeck action done|fail` and `quietdeck actions report`.

outcome.description: What was sent and what came back.

ActionTemplate.description: What a rule allows: action types, and for forwards, resumes and new sessions, the target.

ActionType.description: An action's type alone: the `type` tag, the names `runner.eligible` and project policies use.

AgentStatus.description:
herdr's `agent_status`, as each node forwards it.

- `idle`: waiting for input, and the person has seen its last turn.
- `done`: idle, with a finished turn nobody has looked at yet (herdr's blue dot).
- `working`: running a turn.
- `blocked`: waiting on the person: a permission prompt, a question (herdr's red dot).
- `unknown`: herdr can't tell, or the agent isn't running.

oneOf.description: An option of an `<Ask>`, or its Other text.

What the person says about a `<Default>`: usually an adjustment or an addition, and the start or the next
message of its thread.
The agent's reply in a default's thread (`quietdeck report reply`).

ApiError.description: Every error the REST API returns, with an HTTP status.

ApproveAll.description:
Approve All: every card on screen with its decision (unmentioned means yes, so the app sends approve for each
card the person didn't change), and the timeline entries on screen, which move to History.

single.description: One default's own Approve rather than Approve All: the same undo window, but no Inbox snapshot in History.

ApproveReport.description:
Approve All for the Inbox report: the deck works out the cards itself, those named by each `<Default>` the person
didn't change on this version of the report, so every frontend approves the same way. `report_version` is the
version on screen: a newer one is refused, to be read first.

timeline.description: The timeline entries on screen, which move to History.

Approving.description: What Approve All did: nothing is released until `release_at`, and Undo with `batch` cancels it until then.

cards.description: The cards with a decision in this batch.

setup_needed.description: No passkey is registered yet: the first one needs a setup code from the deck's container.

BlockedPrompt.description:
A blocked prompt: one of the harness's own menus (Claude Code's question form, a permission prompt, a plan to
approve) waiting in a session, as Fleetlayer reads it (`meta.prompt`). The Work tab shows it as a form; the answer
goes back through Fleetlayer.

at.description: When it appeared, as Fleetlayer gives it.

id.description: Fleetlayer's ID for this prompt: stable while it shows, new for every prompt. An answer names it.

options.description: A permission or plan prompt's choices.

questions.description: A question form's questions, in order.

tool.description: A permission prompt's tool, by name, and a short form of its input.

Caller.description: Who the deck thinks is calling.

oneOf.description: An agent (or a shell) on a node, with a session token.
A node itself (its runner), with the node token.
The owner in a browser, signed in with a passkey: `device` is that passkey's name.

Card.description: A card as the deck serves it.

account.description: An account label from deck config.

action_records.description: The current version's actions, in order.

auto_grant.description:
Ask for an automatic action under this grant: the deck runs `rules match`, and stores the card as automatic
only when it allows.

excerpt.description:
The email's own words for the Inbox's details pane, as plain text: the newest message verbatim, or a thread as
one line per message (`Mary: Did we update this for Compass?`). Leave out quoted replies, signatures and
footers. The pane shows the first lines. On an account whose rules keep customers' data out of other
systems, leave out end users' personal data and document contents, as stories and forwards do.

facts.description: Key facts shown under the summary, each `{"label": "Amount", "value": "$1,200"}`.

keep_in_inbox.description: Nothing touches the thread (a newsletter the person reads themselves).

last_message_at.description: When that message arrived. A thread left for later takes a new card only for a message newer than that.

last_message_ref.description: The newest message the card was prepared on, for freshness checks.

list_id.description: The `List-Id` header, for strict rules and the learning loop.

needs_agent.description: The agent wants to carry the card out itself, whatever the runner could do.

pending.description:
The person's decision on this version while it waits out the undo window: the card still reads `open` until
the batch is released (or undone, when this goes away).

rule_ref.description: The rules.md row the agent used.

summary.description:
What the email is, in a few words: the Inbox shows it on one line beside the proposed action. Lead with the kind
of email and leave out who sent it and what their company does unless the person needs that to decide:
"Sales pitch: card dunning", "Water bill, direct debit", "Customer asks how webhook retries work". Facts and
drafts carry the rest.

thread_key.description:
The thread's ID as the mail service gives it: Gmail's thread ID, exactly (`19a4f0c2b7e1d3a5`), with no account
or service prefix (the account is its own field). One card per account and thread; a forward without a
`source` names the thread by it.

to.description:
Which of the person's addresses the newest message went to (an alias such as `hello@example.com` when that's
where it arrived). The Inbox shows it with the sender; without it, the account's address stands in.

auto.description: With `auto_grant`: what `rules match` said. A denied card is stored as a normal card.

replaced.description: True when it replaced the content of the thread's open card.

CardDecision.description: The person's decision on one card version, as the web app sends it.

fields.description: The actions as the person edited them, replacing the proposed ones. Absent means as proposed.

text.description: An adjustment or comment: free text makes it the agent's decision.

version.description: The version on screen. A card that has a newer version by the time the decision is released is skipped.

CardInput.description: `quietdeck card add`: what an agent posts. The posting session comes from its token.

account.description: An account label from deck config.

auto_grant.description:
Ask for an automatic action under this grant: the deck runs `rules match`, and stores the card as automatic
only when it allows.

last_message_at.description: When that message arrived. A thread left for later takes a new card only for a message newer than that.

last_message_ref.description: The newest message the card was prepared on, for freshness checks.

needs_agent.description: The agent wants to carry the card out itself, whatever the runner could do.

rule_ref.description: The rules.md row the agent used.

thread_key.description:
The thread's ID as the mail service gives it: Gmail's thread ID, exactly (`19a4f0c2b7e1d3a5`), with no account
or service prefix (the account is its own field). One card per account and thread; a forward without a

to.description:
Which of the person's addresses the newest message went to (an alias such as `hello@example.com` when that's
where it arrived). The Inbox shows it with the sender; without it, the account's address stands in.

CardResolution.description: `quietdeck card resolve`: the agent's recheck found the card needs nothing more.

oneOf.description: The thread is no longer in the inbox: the card moves to History.

Someone handled it (the person replied, a session mentioned it): the card moves to the archive list with
the note, which the person reads.
The agent rechecked it and it still stands.

CardSection.description: Where a card sits in the Inbox.

oneOf.description: What the person needs to look at: a reply in their name, money, a decision, something only they can do.

Routine mail Approve All just handles, one line each: an archive, with at most a label or a one-line
unsubscribe reply ("Unsubscribe, thanks.") before it. Sales pitches and FYI mail go here.

Catchup.description: "Since your last message": a short account of what happened after the anchor, for the chat view's header.

anchor.description: None when the transcript has no real message from the person.

offset.description: The transcript size `text` was written from.

stale.description: The transcript has grown since `offset`: this text is served now, and a new one is being written.

CatchupAnchor.description:
The newest message from the person that the noise filter accepts as real (not a wake-up, tool output, compaction
or slash command). The chat view opens here.

end.description: Byte offset just past the message's line in the transcript.

uuid.description: The transcript record's `uuid`, when it has one.

Ceremony.description:
A WebAuthn ceremony in progress: `options` goes to `navigator.credentials`, and the result comes back with
`ceremony`.

options.description: WebAuthn options as JSON: pass them to `navigator.credentials.create()` (registering) or `.get()` (signing in).

CeremonyFinish.description: The browser's answer to a ceremony.

credential.description: The WebAuthn credential as JSON, from `navigator.credentials.create()` or `.get()`.

Changed.description:
One message on the event stream (`GET /api/v1/events`): what changed, so it refetches that. Never the data
itself.

oneOf.description: Pings, their feedback and thread watches.
Devices that take pushes.
The Drafts and Sent tabs.
The documents (tabs) and their settings.
The person's marks on sessions: ignored, parked.
The stream fell behind: refetch everything.

ChatReply.description: `quietdeck chat reply`: the agent's answer to the person's chat in the Inbox, shown as a toast.

on.description: What it's on, in a line: the entry's text, or the card's subject.

CommentAdd.description:
The person comments on a timeline entry or a History row. It reaches the agent like an adjustment, and anything
it proposes comes back as a card.

CommentTarget.description: What a comment is on: a timeline entry, or a card in History.

Criteria.description: A strict rule's criteria. A sender criterion needs the card to report DMARC or DKIM passing.

Decide.description:
One card's own decision outside Approve All, which takes effect at once: `later`, `move_up` or `move_down` only.
Approving, editing and adjusting a card go through Approve All (`POST /api/v1/decisions/approve-all`, with
`single: true` for one card), so they get the undo window.

Decision.description: A decision on one card version.

fields.description: The person's edits: the actions as approved, when they changed any.

text.description: The person's adjustment or comment. Free text makes the decision the agent's.

DecisionKind.description: The kinds of decision the person makes on a card.

DeckInfo.description: `GET /api/info`: what agents and the web app need to know about this deck.

actions.description:
Quietdeck solo: the actions its runner carries out once the person approves them. A card proposing another is
refused when posted. Absent on other decks.

commit.description: The release running: the commit it was built from (scripts/build-images passes it), or None for a local build.

solo.description:
Quietdeck solo: the deck on the person's own machine. The Inbox then polls `/api/solo/health` and warns when
the runner or its agent is failing.

started_at.description: When this deck started: with rolling deploys, when the release went live (or the deck last restarted).

oneOf.description: Handed to the session's own messaging socket.
Sent through the orchestrator (herdr: `herdr agent prompt`).
Handed to the runner's headless agent (Quietdeck solo), which reads it in the turn it starts or its next one.

name.description: What the person calls it, shown as its sub-tab: free text.

position.description: Its order among the documents, lowest first; top-level tabs follow their first document.

tab.description: The top-level tab it sits under: free text ("Inbox", "Work").

writer_node.description:
The agent that writes it: an agent's report commands go to the document it writes. None: any agent may (the
Inbox, as before documents).
The agent that writes it (both or neither).

DocumentEdit.description: A change to a document: only the fields given change. `clear_writer` makes it writable by any agent.

clear_writer.description: Any agent may write it from now on.

oneOf.description: Mail: cards about email threads, an archive part with Archive all, and a new report per round.

Sessions: entries about the person's agents, an FYI part that Approve All clears, and one report that's never
replaced, only kept up to date and pruned.

name.description: The machine's name on the deck: letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.

token.description: Shown once. The node keeps it in a file only its user can read.

Fact.description: One fact on a card: an amount, a date, a reference.

History.description: `quietdeck history --since`: what happened since the calling session last looked.

cards.description: Cards whose state or actions changed in that time.

comments.description:
The person's comments on this session's timeline entries and History rows, not picked up before. Empty on
the History screen.

snapshots.description: The Inbox document as it was at each Approve All in that time. Only on the History screen.

HitSource.description: Where a "who has this ID?" hit came from.

HookCreate.description: `quietdeck hooks create`: an agent proposes an endpoint; it receives nothing until the person approves it.

label.description: What it's for, as the person reads it ("Ops alerts").

to.description: The session its events go to, as `<tab>@<node>` ("alerts@server").

HookCreated.description: What `hooks create` answers: the endpoint and its URL, shown this once.

HookEndpoint.description: One endpoint, as Settings and `hooks list` show it. The secret is never shown again after creation.

approved_at.description: None until the person approves it: until then it receives nothing (404).

last_failure.description: The latest time its owner couldn't be reached (the events went to the triage agent instead).

proposed_by.description: Who proposed it (`<tab>@<node>`), when an agent did.

HookKind.description: How the deck reads what arrives.

oneOf.description: Any JSON (or text): a title is taken from the usual fields. Lenient, for Gatus, which doesn't escape its JSON.
Alertmanager's `webhook_configs` format: one event per alert, firing and resolved.

Inbox.description:
The Inbox, for one account or all of them. Nothing here is a count: `has_later` only says whether to show the
Later link.

approving.description: The batch still in its undo window, if any.

finished_cards.description:
Cards the report names that were carried out after an approval (done, or done by a rule): their defaults keep
the green check on every device and after the report changes, without the browser having to remember.

last_agent_at.description: When an agent last posted a card or took decisions. The Inbox shows it only when it's over an hour ago.

presence.description: Whether the person is reading the Inbox, and what the runner holds meanwhile.

report.description: The triage agent's current report, which the Inbox shows in place of the cards.

rule_offers.description: Cards whose target's tab had grants archived when its earlier session closed.

running.description: Whether any approved action is still waiting or running, for Stop.

card_id.description: The card that proposes it, while it's proposed.

kind_state.description: What the kind's create step left behind, such as the Gmail filter's ID.

queue_position.description: Its place in the queue, for an exclusive kind.

message.description: What happened, in a sentence: approved at once, waiting on a card, queued.

LeaseKindInfo.description: What a lease kind says about itself, for the CLI's help and the Settings screen.

slots.description: Slots per resource with a queue, or none for a kind any number of sessions can hold at once.

LeasePattern.description: A Gmail filter the person approved: the same filter on the same account needs no new proposal.

confirmed_by_card_id.description: The card that approved it; none when an agent made it with proposals switched off.

LeaseRegister.description: The kind's create step is done: `quietdeck lease register <id>` with what it left behind.

idle_minutes.description: Ends once the holder has been idle or offline this long. Default 30 minutes.

resource.description: What's leased. For a gmail-filter, the account; for a heavy-build slot, the machine (default: the holder's).

LeasesView.description: The leases list: what's held, queued, waiting or overdue, recent ones, and the approved filters.

MailBadges.description: The counts on the Inbox page's tabs.

drafts.description: How many drafts there are now.

inbox.description: Emails waiting for the person's approval: the distinct threads across the open cards.

sent.description: Sent messages new since the person last opened the Sent tab.

MailRow.description: A row on the Drafts or Sent tab.

at.description: When it was written or sent (Gmail's internal date).

card_id.description: The card whose draft or reply this is, when the deck made it.

draft_id.description: Gmail's draft ID, for a draft (its message ID changes with every save).

new.description: New since the person last opened this tab.

posted_by.description: The session that posted that card.

oneOf.description: The overseer leaves the session out of Work, unless it's blocked on a prompt.

The person put the session's work aside: its entries show in the collapsed Parked part, until `until` or until
unparked.

MatchRequest.description: `quietdeck rules match`: may this card be carried out without the person?

MessageRef.description: A message in a mail thread: what a forward is about.

MessagesPage.description: `quietdeck messages`: messages after the caller's last read (`new`), or after a message ID.

more.description: More messages wait after these: ask again.

MoveLink.description: One end of a move, as `sessions show` prints it: the session on the other end and the handoff between them.

to.description: `tab` or `tab@node`. The node is optional when the tab name is unique across nodes.

NodeRow.description: A node as the deck serves it.

no_handler.description:
The action types the runner handed to its agent for lack of a handler, most often first: candidates for the
next handler. Types only, no counts.

this_device.description: The passkey this browser signed in with.

PendingDecision.description: A decision in its undo window (`Card.pending`).

batch.description: The Approve All batch: `POST /api/v1/decisions/undo` with it cancels the decision.

release_at.description: When the batch is released to the runner.

feedback.description: "Don't ping for this again", with the person's words (empty when they left no note).

PingFeedback.description: "Don't ping for this again", with an optional note for the agent that sent it.

reason.description: The agent's one line on why this can't wait a few hours.

thread_key.description: Repeats for the same thread collapse into one notification.

PingsView.description: The Rules screen's pings: the last seven days' against the weekly budget, which suppresses nothing.

last_week.description: Pings sent in the last seven days.

Presence.description: What the deck knows about the person reading, and what the runner holds meanwhile.

held.description:
New items the runner holds until the person is idle, e.g. "2 Work, 1 in Ops alerts (Matrix)".
None when nothing waits.

PresenceBeat.description: `POST /api/presence`: the Inbox page's heartbeat. `active: false` when the tab is hidden or closed.

device.description: One ID per browser tab, so one tab going idle doesn't end another's activity.

ProjectPolicy.description: A project's autonomy policy, from deck.yaml.

PromptAnswer.description: One question's answer: an option, several (a multiple-choice question), or free text.

PromptAnswerSend.description: The person's answer to a blocked prompt, from the Work tab.

answers.description: One per question, in order; one for a permission or plan prompt.

prompt.description: The prompt's ID, so an answer to a prompt that's gone is refused rather than typed into the next one.

session.description: The session: `<session ID>@<node>`, as the deck names it.

n.description: What to answer to pick it.

other.description: It takes a free-text answer too.

PushConfig.description: Web push on this deck: the VAPID public key a browser subscribes with, or none when push is off.

last_ok_at.description: When a push last reached it.

PushSubscribe.description: A browser's push subscription (`PushSubscription.toJSON()`, flattened), with a name for the device.

ReadingRule.description:
A "while I'm reading" rule: an item that matches every condition it sets gets through while the person reads.
Conditions left out match anything; a rule must set at least one.

account.description: The mail account, or the Matrix room's name.

from.description: The sender contains this (case doesn't matter): `@alertmanager:`, `no-reply@accounts.google.com`.

label.description: The item carries this Gmail label.

name.description: What it's for, as the Rules screen shows it ("Critical alerts").

text_regex.description: An RE2 regular expression the subject and text are matched against: `(?i)\(critical\)`.

ReadingRuleInput.description:
A "while I'm reading" rule: an item that matches every condition it sets gets through while the person reads.
Conditions left out match anything; a rule must set at least one.

account.description: The mail account, or the Matrix room's name.

from.description: The sender contains this (case doesn't matter): `@alertmanager:`, `no-reply@accounts.google.com`.

label.description: The item carries this Gmail label.

name.description: What it's for, as the Rules screen shows it ("Critical alerts").

text_regex.description: An RE2 regular expression the subject and text are matched against: `(?i)\(critical\)`.

oneOf.description: Written by the node's summaries module.
Imported once from claude-summarizer's index.json and Markdown updates.

RegisterStart.description:
Start registering a passkey. Signed in, it adds one for this device; with a setup code (from
`quietdeck-server setup-code`), it registers the first one, or recovers a deck whose passkeys are all lost.

device_name.description: What to call this passkey in Settings ("MacBook", "iPhone").

Released.description:
A released decision with the card it approves, as the runner and `quietdeck decisions take` get it. `actions` is
exactly what was approved, with the person's edits applied.

changes.description:
The person's changes to this card's default in the Inbox, oldest first, in his own words: carry them out
along with the actions.

handoff_reason.description: Why the runner handed it over, when it did.

answers.description: The person's answers and changes on this report, oldest first.

cards_not_in_report.description:
Open cards (waiting on the person, handed off or failed) that no `<Default>` names: the Inbox points at the
Cards screen for them, and `report set` lists them for the agent.

changes.description: The latest changes, newest last (at most 20): the Inbox toasts new ones.

document_id.description: The document it's on (`GET /documents`); 1 is the Inbox.

finished.description:
The agent said nothing on it waits for the person any more (`quietdeck report done`): the Inbox shows "All
done." until the agent edits it or starts the next one.

version.description: Goes up with every edit; an edit names the version it was made from.

about.description: The question or the default's text, so the agent reads the answer without the report.

cards.description:
For an answer to an `<Ask cards="…">`: the cards it's about. The Inbox shows it in the thread of the default
that names them.

control.description: The `<Ask>`'s id, or for a `<Default>` its id or `cards` value.

picked_up.description: The agent has it: delivered as a message, or taken with `quietdeck report answers`.

ReportChange.description: One change to the report, for the Inbox's toast and Approve All's settle window.

cards.description: The cards whose defaults this change added or altered.

reply.description: The agent's answer to the person's chat (`quietdeck chat reply`), not a change: `summary` is its text.

summary.description: What changed, in a line: the agent's `--change`, or what the deck worked out.

ReportChat.description: The chat box under the report: plain words straight to the agent that writes it.

ReportReceipt.description: One action's report from `quietdeck actions report`, as the deck took it.

error.description: Why the deck refused this one; absent when it was recorded.

ReportReply.description: `quietdeck report reply`: the agent's answer in a default's thread, which the Inbox shows under it.

to.description:
The default: the `[key]` its messages to you carry (`cards:c_12`, `archive-all`), or a card it names
(`c_12`).

ReportSet.description: `quietdeck report set`: the whole report, as the agent wants it now.

base.description:
The version this edit starts from (`quietdeck report show` prints it), so an edit never overwrites one it
didn't see. Leave it out only for the first report.

change.description:
What this edit changes, in a line, for the toast the person sees ("New: CI failure on web (c_67)").
Left out, the deck works one out from the defaults that changed.

new.description: Start a new report: the current one is finished (everything on it approved or handled).

ReportSnapshot.description:
The Inbox document as it was when the person pressed Approve All, for History: the report with every answer on it,
the cards it named, and the changes and answers given since the report's previous snapshot.

approved.description: How many cards that Approve All approved.

cards.description: The cards the report's defaults named, and the ones Approve All approved, as they were.

round_answers.description: The person's changes and answers since the previous snapshot of this report, oldest first.

ReportSnapshotSummary.description: A snapshot as History lists it.

answers.description: The changes and answers it records.

runner_told.description: Whether a runner on the caller's machine was told. False when none runs for this session.

RoundStatus.description: `quietdeck round status`: where the runner's mail watch is, for the agent it wakes.

checked_at.description: The last time the watch read the mailboxes' history.

runner.description: No runner on the caller's machine runs for this session, or it isn't connected: nothing else is set.

waiting.description: A wake-up went and `round done` hasn't come yet, so no other goes.

builtin.description: Shipped with the deck (the sent-mail grant). The person can turn it off but not delete it.

known_sender_domains.description: A fuzzy match from any other domain is refused.

RuleInput.description: A grant as the person writes it on the Rules screen or from a card ("Auto-approve matches in future").

project.description:
The project whose policy governs every action. Without one, each action's project is found from its target
session's directory or its account.

session_ref.description: The session the grant is tied to: when it closes, the grant is archived. Defaults to the template's target.

oneOf.description:
The agent judges matches from the instruction; the deck checks the grant, the sender's domain, the template
and the policy.
The deck judges matches from the card's fields.

RuleOffer.description:
On a card that forwards to, resumes or starts a session in a tab whose earlier session's grants were archived
when it closed: those grants can move to this card's target.

oneOf.description: Archived when the session it was tied to closed.

RuleStatusChange.description: Archive, restore, or restore tied to another session ("move").

move_to.description: With `active`: tie the grant to this session, and make it the target of its forwards and resumes.

RulesView.description: The Rules screen, and `quietdeck rules list`.

session_starts_per_day.description: Automatic resumes and new sessions allowed in any 24 hours.

Sender.description: The sender as the agent read it.

chunked by local day for the last 30 days and by ISO week before that.

info.description: Build your own frontend for a Quietdeck deck. Every route is under `/api/v1`. Within v1, changes are additive only: new routes, new optional fields in requests, new fields in responses (ignore the ones you don't know) and new enum values (handle the ones you don't know). Anything that would break a client goes in `/api/v2`, and v1 keeps working alongside it. Operations tagged `report` or `presence` (with `x-quietdeck-ui`) belong to the default web app's own screens: a frontend of its own can ignore them, and with the `report` setting off the report's routes answer 404 and the rest of the API works on cards alone. Errors answer `ApiError` with a 4xx or 5xx status.

tags.description: The deck itself. `GET /info` says who you are and carries the settings and accounts a frontend needs to start; `GET /events` is a server-sent event stream naming what changed, so a frontend reloads only that.
tags.name: deck

tags.description: Passkey sign-in for the owner's browsers. The first passkey takes a one-time setup code from the deck's host; signing in sets an HttpOnly cookie, which the `owner` security scheme names.
tags.name: auth

tags.description: Machines enrolled with the deck. A node enrols once with a one-time code, then keeps a WebSocket open (the node protocol, which frontends don't need) and issues session tokens to the agents on it.
tags.name: nodes

tags.description: A card is what an agent proposes about one email thread: a summary, why, and the actions it would take (archive, label, reply, forward and more). One card per thread: posting again for the same thread makes a new version. A decision names the version on screen, so the person never approves something they didn't see.
tags.name: cards

tags.description: The owner's decisions. Approve All sends every card on screen with its decision; the batch waits out the undo window (Settings), then the runner takes it. `undo` cancels a batch inside its window; `stop` holds everything approved that hasn't started.
tags.name: decisions

tags.description: The runner carrying approved actions out: it marks each one started, then reports the results, which finish the card. The round routes tell the woken agent where the mail watch is.
tags.name: actions

tags.description: Read views for a frontend: the Inbox (open cards by section, the unread timeline, the batch in its undo window), Later, and the mail tabs' lists and badges.
tags.name: inbox

tags.description: What happened without a card: automatic actions the agents carried out, History over a time range, the owner's comments on either, pings (agents asking for attention, against a weekly budget) and thread watches.
tags.name: timeline

tags.description: Agent sessions on every node: list and search them, read a transcript or a catch-up, and start, resume, interrupt or close one.
tags.name: sessions

tags.description: Messages between sessions by address (`tab@node`), chat messages the deck keeps for agents to read, and handoffs that move a session's work to a new one.
tags.name: messages

tags.description: Rules decide what may be carried out without asking: a card that matches an active rule skips the Inbox. Reading rules decide what may still arrive while the owner is reading the Inbox.
tags.name: rules

tags.description: Leases are things agents ask for and give back: a Gmail filter while they watch something themselves (proposed, then approved by the owner) or a heavy-build slot on a machine (acquired, queued if busy).
tags.name: leases

tags.description: Webhook endpoints that wake agents. An agent proposes one; it receives nothing until the owner approves it.
tags.name: hooks

tags.description: Web push: the deck's VAPID key, and the browsers subscribed to notifications.
tags.name: push

tags.description: The default web app's report: the triage agent's write-up of the Inbox, its answers, chat and snapshots. A frontend of its own can ignore these (they carry `x-quietdeck-ui: report`), and with the `report` setting off they answer 404.
tags.name: report

tags.description: Documents are the pages agents write and the owner reads, each under a top-level tab: the Inbox (kind `inbox`) on every deck, and others such as a Work page about the owner's agents (kind `work`). An agent's report commands go to the document it writes; `?doc=<slug>` picks one. Session marks are the owner's records about sessions: ignored, or parked until a time.
tags.name: documents

tags.description: Whether the owner is reading the Inbox in the default web app, so the runner holds new items meanwhile (`x-quietdeck-ui: presence`).
tags.name: presence
